expected.note: Roth IRA distribution of $2,413: $1,850 excludable by stipulation; remaining $563 includible as deemed conceded (Rule 34(b)(4)).
expected.snippet: Petitioner did not allege, in her petition or at trial, that she was entitled to exclude the remaining $563 distribution from gross income.

expected.snippet: respondent has conceded the issue, and petitioner is not subject to the additional tax for premature distribution from a retirement plan

expected.note: Burden of production met on substantial understatement (Rule 155 computation to follow).
expected.snippet: Respondent met this burden because the amount of petitioner's understatement for 2015 is substantial.

issues_outside_coverage: Schedule C car and truck expense deduction ($15,813) disallowed for lack of section 274(d) substantiation
Schedule C education expense deduction ($3,221) disallowed
Home office deduction under section 280A disallowed
Section 6751(b)(2)(B) electronic-calculation exception (part of penalty issue)
decisive_judgment_findings: Petitioner's car and truck testimony was vague and her one-page calendar inadequate under section 274(d).
No explanation for the education expense deduction, which appeared duplicated on Schedule A.
No evidence of the nature of business activity in the home or the space used.
Penalty determined by CEAS software without human examiner involvement.
Reliance on preparer not credited: returns inconsistent with her testimony; insufficient effort to assess proper liability.

unscored_items.note: Decision under Rule 155 after concessions; the court gives no final deficiency figure (notice determined $6,186). No value given.
unscored_items.snippet: To give effect to our disposition of the disputed issues, as well as the parties' concessions, see supra note 2, Decision will be entered under Rule 155.
